title: Operation Iron Justice leads to 27 arrests and recovery of trafficking victims in San Diego
text:
Operation Iron Justice leads to 27 arrests and recovery of trafficking victims in San Diego
California Attorney General Rob Bonta announced on July 29 the results of Operation Iron Justice, a three-day sting conducted by the San Diego Human Trafficking Task Force that resulted in 27 arrests for solicitation-related offenses and the recovery of seven adult and two juvenile trafficking victims. The operation took place from July 22 to 24 throughout San Diego County, targeting demand for commercial sexual exploitation during large-scale events.
Attorney General Bonta said, “The ugly truth is that the demand for these illegal services fuels the supply of commercial sex operations and human trafficking. No matter if it’s around large-scale conventions or anywhere else, solicitation is a crime and California stands ready to hold offenders accountable. My office is proud to lead the San Diego Human Trafficking Task Force to confront demand and support survivors. Our ongoing efforts will continue to keep communities safe and achieve meaningful results that protect Californians.”
U.S. Attorney Adam Gordon said, “The San Diego Human Trafficking Task Force works to disrupt sex trafficking in our community at every level — local, state and federal. Operation Iron Justice showcases that tremendous joint effort. We will not hesitate to prosecute traffickers with the available federal charges that carry 10-year and 15-year mandatory minimum sentences.” Kevin Murphy, Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations San Diego, said their participation reflects an unwavering commitment "to identifying victims, holding perpetrators accountable, and working alongside our law enforcement partners to protect the community." Murphy added that recovering both adult and juvenile victims underscores "the importance of coordinated, victim-centered enforcement efforts."
San Diego County District Attorney Summer Stephan said Operation Iron Justice focused on those buying sex: “The message we sent was loud and clear that human beings are not for sale... The arrest of 27 sex buyers during this large-scale gathering sends a clear message that purchasing sex is not a victimless crime...” Stephan highlighted how holding buyers accountable reduces demand.
During Operation Iron Justice, undercover agents contacted suspected buyers who were then arrested for solicitation or related offenses. Those arrested were booked into jail while recovered victims—including a missing sixteen-year-old—were offered access to resources through supportive services. Large gatherings present opportunities both for exploitation as well as raising awareness about crimes such as sex trafficking or forced labor.
Rob Bonta leads the California Attorney General's office, which serves as California’s chief law enforcement authority with statewide jurisdiction; it focuses on enforcing state laws, protecting public rights and safety, advancing civil rights initiatives including consumer protection policies according to the official website.
The DOJ Victims’ Services Unit works with providers across California offering trauma-informed support services for all crime victims including vulnerable populations; more information can be found at oag.ca.gov/victimservices or by calling (877) 433-9069.
